reader.requirement: At 85 literal-2 or identifier-2's content (any USAGE DISPLAY item: alphanumeric, group, integer numeric, reference-modified) is the delimiter character string; with SIZE the complete sending item is moved; a figurative constant delimiter (any spelling, singular or plural, a symbolic character, HIGH-/LOW-VALUE) is a one-character nonnumeric literal, while ALL figuratives and numeric literals are refused (SR1, SR2).

edition-consulted.switches: string-delimited-omitted-2002: at 85 a last sending phrase without DELIMITED is refused COBOL0900 (2002+ implies SIZE)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior over StringEmitter.cs, CobolStringOps.cs, FigurativeConstants.cs: none; StringUnstringBinder uses ctx.Edition only as the diagnostic sink of its reports, no edition comparison.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: an omitted trailing DELIMITED phrase is refused at 85 and implies SIZE at 2002+; delimiter semantics are the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf02_03 covers SIZE, a literal and a two-character identifier delimiter, SPACE and ZERO delimiters; not exercised: plural figuratives, symbolic characters, HIGH/LOW-VALUE, group SIZE, numeric identifier-2, reference-modified identifier-2, ALL/numeric refusals

probes.expected: group SIZE moves all 6 chars; numeric DN '2' delimits; SPACES/ZEROES one char; symbolic char delimiter; HIGH/LOW one char; S5(4:1) delimits

probes.printed: COBOL1757 DELIMITED BY 'ALL SPACES' refused; refallq.cob COBOL1757 ALL "B"; refnum2.cob COBOL1626 numeric literal delimiter
probes.expected: SR1 ALL figurative and SR2 numeric literal refused
85 format requires DELIMITED after each sending run

reader.notes: A figurative delimiter renders as new string(Fill(kind), 1), one character in the program collating sequence; SIZE passes a null delimiter so the kernel moves the whole image. Diagnostic texts cite 2023 clause numbers.

refuter.evidence: cite.py 'OK §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR2 the text is in GR2', 'OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR5' (HIGH-VALUE = highest in program collating sequence). Probes at 85: sp1.cob signed S9 identifier-2 delimiter matches its overpunched content ('3 [AB******]'); FUNCTION UPPER-CASE sender (amendment 1) admitted '2 [AB******]'; hv4.cob under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE ALPHABET 256 THRU 1, HIGH-VALUES and LOW-VALUE delimiters stop at a character MOVEd from the same figurative ('1 [AB**]','2 [A***]'); subp.cob subscripted delimiter D(P) evaluated once (§1985:IV.4.3.8 OK) '2 [A*******] 02'; n85.cob N"AB" refused COBOL0900 at 85. hv2/hv3 first looked like HIGH-VALUE was wrong under the reversed alphabet (ORD 65536, U+FFFF), but docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-31.md makes the native set the 65,536 BMP code units, so the unspecified characters follow and U+FFFF is the highest: consistent, not a defect.
